patients.label: 27-year-old pregnant woman found collapsed and pronounced dead on admission; autopsy diagnosis ARVC/D
attribution_limitations: Gestational age is stated as the 11th week of amenorrhea in the case history, as the 11th week of pregnancy in the abstract and as first trimester for the cause of death; weeks counted from amenorrhea versus pregnancy are not reconciled.
The discussion hedges the disease stage and mechanism of death ("probably in the concealed phase", "may have caused strain") as the authors' interpretation.
The discussion says "these tests were not done in this victim during life" after listing generic ECG, imaging and biopsy features of ARVC/D, so which tests are meant is not stated for this patient.

limitations: The source lists no main-article figures, so there is no visual.json; the one supplement image SM1385 (three panels A-C) is reviewed in its supplement sidecars.

The case text cites "Figure S1(A)", "Figure S1(B)" and "Figure S1(C)", but the supplement's own caption title is the filename "Supp_mat_TFSR_Figure_1_1325548.jpg" and no cross-reference or caption links those citations to SM1385; its panel ownership is left unresolved (not attributed by content match).
Discussion sentences are general literature or hedged author interpretation and are not copied to the patient.
No ECG, echocardiography or other in-life cardiac testing is reported for this patient.

claims.text: A 27-year-old apparently healthy Sri Lankan woman, a teacher with no significant past medical or surgical history, conceived three months after stopping the oral contraceptive pill. Urine was positive for human chorionic gonadotropin, and an antenatal visit found her clinical examination, full blood count and urine report normal. She had not complained of breathlessness, chest tightness, syncope or palpitation, and history did not reveal chest pain, and there was no family history of sudden death or ARVC/D.

A medico-legal autopsy found a moderately dilated right ventricle with 1-3 mm wall thickness and epicardial fat 4-5 mm thick infiltrating the myocardium, with an intrauterine foetus, while other cardiac structures were macroscopically normal and no other macroscopic abnormalities were detected.
